caption: 01 · CLAIM — What authority is being asserted?. Name the verb: preserve, exhibit, authenticate, reproduce, license, design, speak for, teach, sell, or change. Avoid the totalizing phrase “protect the legacy.”
credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
alt: Diagram mapping what authority is being asserted? within Who Is Allowed to Interpret a Dead Designer’s Codes?.
rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

crop: native 4:5 diagram; preserve labels and evidence footer
caption: 02 · RECORD — What supports that claim?. Attach corporate appointment, trademark record, license, will, probate order, copyright chain, collection agreement, employment record, oral history, craft evidence, or community protocol as appropriate.
credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
alt: Diagram mapping what supports that claim? within Who Is Allowed to Interpret a Dead Designer’s Codes?.
rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

crop: native 4:5 diagram; preserve labels and evidence footer
caption: 03 · LIMIT — Where does the authority stop?. A museum accession does not appoint a house successor; inherited copyright does not confer craft mastery; corporate title does not erase community memory; cultural legitimacy does not itself transfer a registered asset.
credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
alt: Diagram mapping where does the authority stop? within Who Is Allowed to Interpret a Dead Designer’s Codes?.
rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

crop: native 4:5 diagram; preserve labels and evidence footer
caption: 04 · CONTEST — How can interpretation be challenged and revised?. Publish sources, acknowledge gaps, credit carriers, invite corrections, document dissent, and schedule periodic review rather than presenting succession as final truth.
credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
alt: Diagram mapping how can interpretation be challenged and revised? within Who Is Allowed to Interpret a Dead Designer’s Codes?.
